1) Composite rate anchoring (Section 2.3) — the phrasing suggests a blended "composite" rate will be used for billing in months where bundles are partially used. We need an explicit definition of how that anchor is calculated (token-weighted vs. seat-weighted) and whether usage above the anchor reverts to the standard per-token bands or a blended true-up.

2) Bundle demux / unbundling (Section 4.1) — Novus buys Packaging Bundle A (embeddings + generation credits). Your redline shows an option to "demux" the bundle if a portion of credits are unused for 90 days. We need to understand the operational effect: will unused embeddings roll to a per-unit billing rate, or will they be forfeited? If there is an automatic conversion, what rate applies and does a floor/ceiling apply?

I attached our annotated Exhibit C (Novus_Exhibit_C_v3.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood intends the composite anchor to be a monthly arithmetic average or something else, and provide proposed picklist language for the bundle demux mechanics?

Julia — thanks for the quick read and the annotated PDF. High level answers before Marissa (legal) weighs in:

- Composite anchor: our intent was a token-weighted composite across SKU lines for the invoice period. Practically that means we take total billed tokens across generation + reranking + embedding lines and divide by total token-equivalent units to generate the composite per-token anchor. That anchor is only used for mid-month smoothing; any usage above the committed band triggers the standard banded overage rates on the excess.

- Bundle demux: the current redline proposes an optional conversion of unused bundle credits to per-unit billable credits at a conversion rate equal to the bundle's embedded per-unit equivalent less a 10% stabilization discount, subject to a monthly floor equal to 25% of the original bundle price. We see this as a customer-friendly fallback to avoid forfeiture.

I'll attach a short markup (RNWD_response_markup.docx) with picklist language options (A, B, C) — option A is token-weighted anchor + automatic conversion, option B retains forfeiture but allows one-time grace, option C uses seat-weighted anchor. Legal will recommend which to propose. Marissa — can you review and propose a final wording we can push to Novus?

Best,
Dylan Brooks

Julia — thanks for the note and the redline. I reviewed Procurement's questions and drafted suggested language below for insertion into Exhibit C. This is intended to be narrow and operational to avoid shifting economic terms in the main order form: 

1) Composite Anchor (new Section 2.3.1) — "For purposes of mid-period smoothing, the Composite Rate shall mean the token-weighted average per-token rate computed by dividing Total Billable Tokens for the Billing Period across the Applicable SKUs by the aggregate Token-Equivalent Units billed across those SKUs. Example: if Generation = 1,200,000 tokens at $0.0025/token and Embeddings = 300,000 tokens at an equivalent $0.0010/token, the Composite Rate = ((1,200,000*0.0025)+(300,000*0.0010))/(1,200,000+300,000) = $0.0022 per token. The Composite Rate is used only for smoothing and shall not change the application of banded overage rates to any usage exceeding committed bands."

2) Bundle Conversion (new Section 4.1.3) — provide picklist table: 

- Option A (Automatic Conversion): "Unused bundle credits shall convert to billable per-unit credits on the first day following the Retention Window at a conversion rate equal to the bundle-equivalent per-unit rate less a ten percent (10%) stabilization discount, subject to a Monthly Floor equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of the bundle's original paid value. Converted credits will appear on the invoice as 'Converted Bundle Credits' with the per-unit rate shown."

- Option B (Forfeiture with Carryover): "Up to fifteen percent (15%) of unused bundle credits may be carried forward to the next billing period only once during the Term; any remainder shall be forfeited."

- Option C (Explicit Numeric Conversion): "Unused bundle credits shall convert at a per-unit rate equal to $X per 1,000 tokens (as set forth in the accompanying invoice sample)."

Legal note: we recommend Option A with an explicit example inserted (per the Composite Anchor example) and a completed numeric floor populated to avoid ambiguity. If Novus prefers an explicit dollar-for-dollar numeric rate, we can insert Option C but need confirmation of the $X value (procurement or finance to propose).

Please let us know which Option Novus prefers; if Option C, please provide the $X value for the conversion rate and we will prepare a clean redline for signature.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
